Those numbers were taken when pow_1_3 was powers.rs::cbrt_f64, inline branch-free arithmetic LLVM packed 8-wide. rmath::cbrt (BitExact, bit-identical to glibc on 100% of 2M physical inputs) is an opaque ~9.6 ns/elem call, which stops the grid loop vectorising; explicit SIMD gives it back. Timed jointly with the vxc case (exc has no separate xcvs leg).

gga_x_pbepow:fxc:unpol.note: Rejected on the fingerprint gate despite 1.93x. The cause is NOT the vector pow: `math/examples/pow_exact.rs` compares simd::pow against rmath::pow over 200,000 lanes spanning negative bases and fractional exponents and finds 200,000 identical bit patterns, NaN payloads included. 231 of the other 237 pow-using triples also pass the fingerprint gate. So something else in this 1,280-line fxc body derives a value down a different path in the vector form -- most likely a NaN whose payload IEEE 754 leaves unspecified, the effect AGENTS.md records for deduplicated computations. Not chased further: the tree does not accept a kernel whose bits moved, whatever the reason.
